product.tagline_short: Universal GUI generator for command-line tools
product.tagline_long: ScripTree is an open-source desktop runtime that turns command-line tools into clean GUIs. Point it at an executable and you get a labeled form with dropdowns, file pickers, and checkboxes — no GUI code required. The same runtime powers the ScripTreeApps marketplace.
product.description_paragraph: ScripTree is an open-source desktop runtime (PySide6, Python 3.11+) for turning command-line tools into GUI-driven launchers. A tool is described in a `.scriptree` file (parameters, defaults, environment, capability scopes); ScripTree reads the description, builds a form for it, and runs the tool with `shell=False` and input sanitization on every invocation. Tools can be grouped into `.scriptreetree` trees or arranged as `.scriptreering` desktop cells. The forest workspace pulls everything in a folder together into one persistent layout. The runtime is portable (zip-and-run, no registry, no admin rights) and configuration is INI-based.
what_it_is: GUI launcher for CLI tools, organized as a tree of hexagonal cells (the V3 "forest workspace")
Auto-parser for `--help` output from argparse, click, PowerShell, Windows-style /flag tools, and GNU long-flag tools
Named, reusable per-tool configurations (presets with environment overrides, UI visibility, hidden parameters)
Standalone (single-tool) launcher mode for end-user-facing distribution of one tool at a time
File-based capability permissions — 32 capability files in `permissions/`, NTFS-ACL compatible, secure defaults
Encrypted credentials store for run-as-different-user (XOR pad, immediate zeroization)
Portable: vendored Python + PySide6 in `lib/`, INI settings, zero registry, copy and run
Headless screenshot CLI (`screenshooter.py`) for rendering tools, trees, cells, popup menus, and forest composites as PNG without ever showing a window
what_it_is_not: NOT a sandbox or OS-level isolation layer — the file-based permissions are a discipline, not an enforcement boundary (see `scriptree/core/sanitize.py:45,133`: "warning, not a sandbox")
NOT a bundle-signing platform — there is no cryptographic signature on the runtime's `.scriptree` / `.scriptreetree` files and no signature-verification step at install time
NOT an automatic update delivery service — installs are extract-folder-from-zip; updates are a re-extract by the user (or by the operator of a downstream marketplace)
NOT a rollback service — previous versions must be retained manually by the user; the runtime has no rollback UI or per-app version directory
NOT a process supervisor — ScripTree launches a tool and waits for it; it does not restart, monitor, or daemonize child processes
NOT a network-aware update checker — the runtime does not phone home

host_plugins._comment: Host-application integrations are provided by the `combridge` runtime (bundled at `lib/combridge/`). Each plugin is one named plugin in `combridge/plugins/<Name>/`. Status enum: shipped | planned | not_planned. Only `shipped` plugins may be advertised as supported today.
host_plugins._comment_aspirational: AutoCAD / Inventor / Revit are listed under `not_planned_today` because downstream marketing has sometimes advertised them. No `combridge` plugin exists for any of them; they are not on the runtime roadmap as of this file's `_updated_at`. If/when one is added, move the slug from `not_planned_today` to `planned` (work begun) or `shipped` (in `combridge/plugins/`).

features._comment: Status enum: shipped | planned | not_planned. Marketing surfaces (marketplace, sister site, producer agreement) MUST NOT claim a feature whose status is not `shipped`. Promote a status from `not_planned` to `planned` only when there's a concrete roadmap entry; from `planned` to `shipped` only when the code actually exists.

install_model.distribution: GitHub Releases (portable ZIP) + source clone of `KenM76/scriptree`
install_model._comment_distribution: There is no managed installer, no MSI, no app-store distribution channel today. End-users download the ZIP and extract it.
install_model._comment_verification: No cryptographic signature on the ZIP, no checksum verification by the runtime at extract time, no first-run verifier. Add `verification_at_install: hash` or `signature` only when the runtime ships that code path.
install_model._comment_update: User re-downloads the new ZIP and re-extracts. No in-app updater. The marketplace may notify buyers that a new version exists; that notification is a marketplace feature, not a runtime feature.

marketplace._comment: Where the runtime's commercial surface lives. The runtime itself does not handle catalog, payments, reviews, or refunds — those belong to the marketplace. Marketplace brand identity (palette, fonts, asset paths) stays in the marketplace's own `branding/branding.config.json`; this block only records that a marketplace exists and where it is.

open_source._comment_license: Verified against LICENSE line 1: "MIT License", line 3: "Copyright (c) 2026 Ken M".

version._comment_version: Source: pyproject.toml `project.version`. Major-version cadence is not yet formalized; the runtime ships pre-1.0 alphas as of `_updated_at`.

terminology._comment: Canonical phrases that all marketing/legal surfaces MUST use. Brand-rename safe — these are the OPERATOR (marketplace) attestations, not the runtime's; a fork of the marketplace would replace these values, but the field names are stable.
terminology._comment_attestation_verb: Replaces 'operator-signed' / 'Platform-signed' / 'we sign your bundle'. The runtime does NOT cryptographically sign; the operator (marketplace) attests via ClamAV scan + identity bind + record stamp. 'Attested' is honest where 'signed' implied cryptographic non-repudiation that doesn't exist.
terminology._comment_attestation_noun: Use as a noun phrase: 'each download includes an operator attestation' (not 'a Platform signature').
terminology._comment_what_the_operator_does: Short verb-phrase summary of what the marketplace does to a bundle before it's distributed. Read by the producer-agreement help-section + the help-center 'Trust & Safety' page.
